clue.text: Make up with firm friend stealing pounds

indicators.note: a thief takes something and holds it, so the friend word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a mate is a friend
pounds are enclosures for animals, as pens are

explanation.surface: Someone makes peace with a business pal who has pocketed some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money, but here it means animal enclosures.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate is to offset a loss or shortfall, which is what making up for it means.

clue.text: Quote Lincoln perhaps, changing end for English

indicators.note: changing the end for something swaps the final letter of the word for a new one

blocks.note: Lincoln is an English cathedral city; 'perhaps' marks it as one example
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone repeats Abraham Lincoln's words, with a British twist at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the president, but it is the city in Lincolnshire; swap the Y of CITY for E to get CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a passage is to quote it, both verbs meaning repeat someone's words as evidence or reference.

clue.text: Denote low average

blocks.note: signify, stand for
base, ignoble or stingy
the arithmetic middle value of a set

explanation.surface: A statistician labels some figure as a poor average.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: three separate senses of one four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for signify, an adjective for petty or base, and a noun for an arithmetic average.

clue.text: Oz city, flourishing in shade

blocks.note: the Emerald City is the capital of the Land of Oz in The Wizard of Oz
green can mean verdant and thriving, as growing plants are

explanation.surface: An Australian city is booming in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is a common nickname for Australia, but here it is L. Frank Baum's fictional land.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald green is a particular bright colour, and a shade is a variety of colour.

clue.text: Tool beginning to sink around very bad hole

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
something bad is spoiled or wrong, so these letters are rearranged into a new order
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the abbreviation

blocks.note: the first letter of sink
taken as written
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A digging tool starts to sink into a dreadful pit.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLE is shuffled to HOEL and wrapped around V, making HOVEL, a squalid dwelling; S goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is an implement for digging and moving earth, so it is one example of a tool.

clue.text: Your old subordinate enters making loud noise

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the subordinate word is placed within the other

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
a subordinate is under someone else

explanation.surface: A former junior employee of yours bursts in, very noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the archaic pronoun THY, which holds UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundery describes weather with thunder, which is a booming, roaring sound in the sky.

clue.text: Match house

blocks.note: first meaning: a ...-final, a match in a knockout competition
second meaning: a ...-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a semi is everyday shorthand both for a semi-final and for a semi-detached home.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form serves as a noun for a penultimate sporting round and a dwelling joined to another.

clue.text: Greatly irritate former partner according to returning Greek character

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letter's name is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover
as per means according to
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Your ex, as a Greek friend tells it, drives you up the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA reversed gives ATE, which ends EX + AS PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate someone is to annoy them intensely, a stronger form of irritation.

clue.text: Boaty McBoatface, by majority vote, a way to get people talking

definitions.text: a way to get people talking

blocks.note: first meaning: Boaty McBoatface won a 2016 public poll to name a British polar research ship, a vessel built to cut through ice

blocks.clueFragment: a way to get people talking
blocks.note: second meaning: a game or remark that eases awkwardness among strangers

explanation.surface: A comic name chosen by public vote has become a great conversation starter.
explanation.walkthrough: The online vote chose Boaty McBoatface, though the ship was named RRS Sir David Attenborough and the name went to its submarine; the clue leans on the popular verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a ship that breaks polar ice; the other is an activity that relaxes a group of strangers.

clue.text: Hugely enthusiastic record contained in short weekday tourism lecture

indicators.note: contained in means held inside, so the first pieces sit within the day abbreviation

blocks.note: a rave review is a hugely enthusiastic one
a log is a written record
Tue is the short form of Tuesday

explanation.surface: A gushing account of the week's tourism talk is written up.
explanation.walkthrough: A rave review is a wildly enthusiastic one, which is why 'hugely enthusiastic' can stand for that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelogue is a film or illustrated talk about places visited, i.e. a lecture about travel.

clue.text: Composer, a great experimentalist primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives up its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of Composer
the word a itself
first letter of great
first letter of experimentalist

explanation.surface: A tribute to one composer as the great pioneer of experimental music.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the initials spell the composer it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer famous for chance music and the silent piece 4'33".

clue.text: Aircrews into rolling the other way round

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over and over, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flight crews turning a plane over in a barrel roll, upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link to rolling, but its letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrariwise means conversely or in the opposite manner, i.e. reversed in order or direction.

clue.text: Spy something falling off the roof?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who secretly listens in on others
second meaning, read literally: a drip that drops from the eaves, the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.walkthrough: The word is said to come from people standing under the eaves to hear what was said inside; the question mark flags the punning literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who listens covertly to private conversations is gathering secrets, as an agent would.

clue.text: Half a book about essential short pastry

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts, so the back of the book name is dropped
short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Old Testament
ca is the abbreviation of circa, about
key means essential, as in a key point

explanation.surface: Someone skims half a book on the bare essentials of pastry-making.
explanation.walkthrough: The first six of twelve letters of the biblical book give ECCLES, a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a round flaky pastry filled with currants, named after the Lancashire town.

clue.text: Two politicians welcoming new rite in Mass

indicators.note: a new version of something is remade, so these letters are reworked into a different order
welcoming means taking someone in, so the politicians' letters enclose the reworked word

blocks.note: a Con is a Conservative, and two of them are needed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of MPs make room for a novel ceremony in a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' wants to be the church service; it is the definition, a solid lump. Con is short for a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A concretion is a hard solid lump formed by accumulation, such as a stone in the body.

clue.text: Classy girl becomes flashy or gloomy

indicators.note: becomes says one thing turns into another, so the girl inside the first word is replaced

blocks.note: taken as written
a lass is a girl
loud clothes are flashy and garish

explanation.surface: A refined young woman turns either showy or depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is hiding inside the word Classy itself, so it is that word, not a name, that changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy weather is overcast and dark, and gloomy likewise describes dim, dull skies or moods.

clue.text: Spies seizing author, abandoning western rules

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing and holding, so the spies' letters wrap around the other piece
abandoning means leaving behind, so the abbreviation is dropped from the word

blocks.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
an author is a writer
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents kidnap a novelist, ignoring the West's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards used for judging, and rules are principles laid down for the same purpose.

clue.text: Work quietly in theatre strike

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: Actors quietly down tools in a theatre walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: Op is short for opus, a musical work, and p stands for piano, the musical direction for soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt to work by employees, which is what an industrial strike is.

clue.text: Cost following fabric rip

blocks.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a placing word: the cost comes after the fabric
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: The price of a damaged piece of cloth after it tore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' sets the order, so the pieces are read in the reverse of the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear flesh or skin, so it is a verb meaning tear open.

clue.text: Rubbish story, no answer to gossip

indicators.note: no says something is absent, so the abbreviation is removed from the word

blocks.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff
a tale is a story
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A rubbish story with no reply ends up as mere rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattle is to chatter idly or tell tales about others, which is what gossip means as a verb.

clue.text: Volunteer shared time off at university

indicators.note: off means removed, so the abbreviation is taken away from the word

blocks.note: a joint account is shared
T is the abbreviation for time
to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Students sharing a holiday from college sign up for some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time off' reads as a holiday, but it means remove T from JOINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up is to enlist in the armed forces, and volunteer as a verb means enlist willingly.

clue.text: Like some sound that's unsettled Chinese troop

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed and out of place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noise made by a troubled company of Chinese soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereophonic sound comes through two channels to give a spatial effect, so it describes certain audio.

clue.text: Clydeside library's housing unusual food shop

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the run of letters sits within the words before it

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Glasgow library has a strange shop inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Clydeside is the area along the River Clyde in Glasgow. The letters run across 'ClydesiDE LIbrary's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen sells prepared and imported foods, often ones hard to find in an ordinary grocer.

clue.text: Unexpectedly discover internet sleuth?

blocks.note: first meaning: catch sight of, spot
second meaning, punningly split

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: e- as in e-mail plus a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to glimpse or notice something, often by chance or at a distance.

clue.text: Dry drinking establishment: try banning all bishops

indicators.note: banning all means excluding every one, so each instance of the letter is struck out

blocks.note: a bar is a place to drink
a bid is an attempt
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A teetotal pub that keeps clergy out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like describing the pub, but it is the definition; BAR + BID lose both Bs.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land has little or no rain, so it is parched and without moisture.

clue.text: Just insane excited exuberance

indicators.note: something excited is agitated and stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wild, crazy high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Jauntiness is a lively, cheerful self-confidence, close in sense to high-spirited enthusiasm.

clue.text: Eagle picked up vase

indicators.note: picked up is what a microphone or listener does, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an urn is a vase, and the two words are said the same way

explanation.surface: A bird of prey snatches up a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' pictures talons lifting something, but it signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large bird of prey of northern coasts.

clue.text: A shame about Roman law intricacy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shame word goes round the legal term

blocks.note: a means per, as in five pounds a head
a pity is a shame, as in what a pity
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: Someone regrets how complicated the law of ancient Rome is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' standing for per is the usage in prices such as two pounds a kilo.
explanation.definitionFit: Perplexity can mean complexity or entanglement, a tangled state that is hard to follow.
